prs.title: fix(expect): pass current equality testers to `expect.extend` asymmetric matchers
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/6825
- related to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11296

#6825 forwarded the outer matcher's equality testers to built-in asymmetric matchers, but not to ones created via `expect.extend` (e.g. `expect.toBeOneOf`). This PR forwards them there too.

```ts
class Stock { constructor(public type: string) {} }

// already fails since #6825
expect([new Set()]).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([new Set(['x'])]))
expect([new Stock('x')]).toStrictEqual(expect.arrayContaining([{ type: 'x' }]))

// passes before this PR, fails after
expect(new Set()).toEqual(expect.toBeOneOf([new Set(['x'])]))
expect(new Stock('x')).toStrictEqual(expect.toBeOneOf([{ type: 'x' }]))
```

Non-asymmetric `expect(new Set()).toBeOneOf([new Set(['x'])])` still passes (i.e. broken), but that's left for #11296.

prs.title: fix(vm): don't reuse scripts across vite environments
prs.author: MO2k4
prs.body:
### Description

Written by an AI agent (Claude) on behalf of @MO2k4, who has reviewed it.

The vm pools cache compiled scripts of inlined modules per worker (#10744), keyed only by module id. A worker can run both `jsdom` files (`client` environment) and `node` files (`ssr` environment), which transform the same id differently: for example, optimized deps resolve to `deps/` in one and `deps_ssr/` in the other. The second environment then evaluates the first one's code. This shows up as `vi.mock` not being applied and as duplicate module instances (`instanceof` failing), and it depends on the order files land on workers.

The cache now also stores the code and reuses a script only when the code matches, the same way `CodeCache` already works for externalized modules.

Bisected on a real suite: `de63174f5` is clean and `d8b040c63` (#10744) fails. With this change, that suite is green in 3 of 3 runs, compared with 13–31 failures per run on 5.0.2.

Resolves #11289

prs.title: fix(ui): remove duplicate browser-open call opening two tabs (fix #11356)
prs.author: feastyr69
prs.body:
### Description

Fixes `vitest --ui` always opening two browser tabs.

**Bug:** two separate code paths were both trying to open the browser.
- `resolveConfig.ts` sets `rootViteConfig.server.open` to the UI's URL. When the Vite cluster server is created and `server.listen()` runs, Vite sees this truthy `server.open` and opens the browser itself.

-  `create.ts` then *also* explicitly called `vitest.vite.openBrowser()` , a second redundant open on top of Vite's own automatic one. Neither call suppressed the other, so every `vitest --ui` launch opened two tabs instead of one.

**Fix:** removed the redundant explicit `vitest.vite.openBrowser()` call in `create.ts`. Vite's own `server.listen()` already opens the correct UI URL via the `server.open` config set in `resolveConfig.ts`, so nothing else needs to trigger it.

Resolves #11356

prs.title: fix(api): publish the api token atomically
prs.author: umairnawaz333
prs.body:
### Description

`resolveTokenFromPath` checks `existsSync` and then reads, and publishes the token with a plain `writeFileSync`. Both halves are visible to a concurrent process: the file exists as soon as it is created but before it is written, so a second process reads `''`, and `.trim()` keeps it. That empty token reaches the browser client as `"0"`, the websocket handshake rejects it, and the run sits on the 60s connection timeout without executing tests.

This changes both halves:

- the read goes straight to `readFileSync` and treats empty contents as "no token", so a partial or truncated file is regenerated rather than accepted
- the write goes to a temp file in the same directory and is published with `linkSync`, which fails with `EEXIST` when another process got there first. The loser adopts the token that was actually stored instead of overwriting it, so every process agrees on one token. `renameSync` would publish atomically too, but it clobbers, and then the process that lost the race keeps a token the file no longer holds — the same mismatch in a different place.

A 12-process harness against the current code returns two different tokens in roughly a quarter of rounds, one of them not matching the file on disk; with this change 8/8 rounds agree.

Resolves #11315

This was written with assistance from Claude Code.

prs.title: fix(browser): close the mock route interception race (fix #8339)
prs.author: cplieger
prs.body:
### Description

Fix for #8339, the random `vi.mocked(...).mockX is not a function` / `[Function x] is not a spy` flake in browser mode. The root cause was traced in the issue thread.

Mock routes are added per test file and unrouted when the file ends, so the context's route count crosses zero between two mocking files and Playwright turns CDP request interception off and back on around it. Chromium acks `Fetch.enable` before interception is live, so a module request in that window is served the real module, and the ES module registry keeps it for the rest of the file. Only chromium is affected; the race was never reproduced on firefox or webkit.

The fix arms interception once per context, at the first `vi.mock` registration: one permanent probe route keeps the route count above zero, and the registration resolves only after a `fetch()` of the probe URL comes back with the route's header, so interception is provably live before the mocked import runs. If that cannot be verified within 5s the registration rejects with an error naming the issue instead of mocks silently not applying, and the next mocking file retries.

Suites without mocks get nothing: no route, no `Fetch.enable`, browser cache stays on. Firefox and webkit are unchanged.

Resolves #8339

prs.title: fix(browser): allow toHaveTextContent without arguments
prs.author: nomadical
prs.body:
### Description

Makes the `text` argument of `toHaveTextContent` optional. Called without arguments the matcher asserts the element has some text content, so `.not.toHaveTextContent()` asserts it is empty (the shape agreed in the issue).

Types and docs updated to match.

Resolves #8997

Claude Code assisted with the investigation and the draft; I reviewed and tested the change.
